chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Abū al-Jārūd, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Whoever renews a grave or fashions an image has exited Islam.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: Our companions have differed regarding the transmission of this report and its interpretation. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār said: It is “jaddada” with jīm and nothing else; and he used to say that it is not permissible to renew a grave and plaster all of it after days have passed over it and after it had already been plastered initially. But if a deceased person dies and his grave is plastered, then it is permissible that the rest of the graves be repaired without being renewed. Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: Rather it is “ḥaddada qabran” with the undotted ḥāʾ, meaning by it one who raises a grave into a hump. Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī said: Rather it is “jaddatha qabran” with jīm and thāʾ, and he did not explain what it means. It is possible that what is meant by this narration is the prohibition of making the grave, another time, a grave for another human being, because al-jadath means the grave, so it is possible that the verb is derived from it. Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Bābawayh said: Rather it is “jaddada” with jīm. He said: Its meaning is the exhumation of a person’s grave, because whoever exhumes a grave has indeed renewed it and made it in need of renewal, and has made it a jadath. Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn said: Renewal according to the meaning held by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, and delimiting with the undotted ḥāʾ according to what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh held, and what al-Barqī said, that it is “jaddatha,” all of it falls within the meaning of the hadith. And whoever opposes the Imam in renewal, raising into a hump, and exhumation, and deems any of that lawful, has exited Islam. Our Shaykh Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān, may Allah have mercy on him, used to say: The report is with khāʾ and two dāls, and that is derived from His, Exalted is He, saying:
“Slain were the companions of the trench.”

And al-khadd is a split; it is said: “I split the earth with a khadd,” meaning, I cleft it. According to these readings, the prohibition would apply to splitting open the grave, either so that someone may be buried in it, or by way of exhumation, according to what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī held. All that we have mentioned of the variant transmissions and meanings is possible, and Allah knows best what is intended, and what was meant by the one from whom the report issued, عليه السلام.

key_terms.التَّسْنِيمِ: raising a grave into a hump-like form
key_terms.النَّبْشِ: exhumation; opening or digging up a grave
key_terms.الْأُخْدُودِ: the trench; cited from the Qur'an to explain another possible reading
key_terms.الْجَدَثَ: grave; cited as a lexical basis for one reading of the report
key_terms.تَجْدِيدُ: renewal or replastering; discussed as grave restoration after time has passed
key_terms.جَدَّدَ: renewed or restored; here discussed as a possible technical expression concerning graves
key_terms.قَبْرًا: a grave; the central legal subject of the report
key_terms.مَثَّلَ مِثَالًا: fashioned an image; making a formed representation

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith "مَنْ جَدَّدَ قَبْرًا أَوْ مَثَّلَ مِثَالًا" mean in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام is followed by an extended discussion among Shia scholars over the exact wording and meaning of the phrase concerning graves. The report is treated as a legal text dealing with grave renovation, raising graves, or exhumation, with the emphasis that knowingly opposing the Imam’s ruling and deeming such acts lawful is what is described as exiting Islam. The passage is also important for hadith transmission, because it preserves multiple readings and scholarly attempts to reconcile them.
